description: These braised beef short ribs are layered with complex Chinese flavors, including soy, orange, five-spice powder, ginger, and more. Serve them on mashed potatoes one day; shred the meat and fold it into awesome tacos the next.
notes: Make sure to get the English cut of short ribs, which leaves one large rib bone in each piece of beef; flanken-cut ribs should be avoided, since each piece of beef will have several cross-cut bones in it.

brief: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C) or plug in a slow cooker.
steps.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Alternatively, plug in a slow cooker.

brief: Pat short ribs dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat {{2 tbsp}} oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown short ribs in batches and transfer to a plate.
Pour off all but {{2 tbsp}} fat.
steps.text: Pat short ribs dry with clean towels. Lightly season short ribs on both sides with salt and more generously with black pepper. Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add short ribs in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid crowding the pot. Brown well on all sides, then transfer to a plate and set aside. Pour off all but {{2 tbsp}} fat from Dutch oven.

brief: Add onion, ginger, garlic, and five-spice powder.
Cook and stir until softened and fragrant, about 4 minutes.
steps.text: Add onion, ginger, garlic, and five-spice powder to Dutch oven and cook over medium-high heat, stirring, until onions are slightly softened and fragrant, about 4 minutes.

brief: Add orange zest strips, {{1/4 cup}} orange juice, rice wine, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, chili paste, hoisin, and stock.
Stir to combine and return ribs and juices to the pot.
steps.text: Add strips of orange zest and {{1/4 cup}} orange juice along with rice wine or sherry, soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, honey, chili paste, hoisin, and chicken stock or water. Stir to combine. Return ribs to Dutch oven along with any accumulated juices. (Alternatively, add ribs, vegetables, and liquid to slow cooker.)

brief: Cook on high in slow cooker until tender, 6 to 8 hours.
steps.text: If Using a Slow Cooker: Set slow cooker to high and cook until meat is tender and frees easily from bones, 6 to 8 hours.

brief: Bring to a boil, cover, and transfer to oven.
Braise until tender, about 3 hours, removing lid for the last 20 minutes.
steps.text: If Using a Dutch Oven: Bring contents to a boil, cover, and transfer to oven. Cook until short ribs are tender, about 3 hours. Check periodically during cooking process and add more stock or water if needed. Remove lid during the last 20 minutes of cooking. The meat should be very tender but not completely falling apart.

brief: Remove and keep warm the ribs, strain and defat the liquid, and return sauce to pot.
Stir in remaining {{1/4 cup}} orange juice and reduce to {{3 cups}} if needed.
Thicken with cornstarch mixture in {{1 tbsp}} increments.
steps.text: When meat is cooked, remove ribs and keep warm in a serving dish. Strain braising liquid into a fat separator (or strain braising liquid, then spoon off as much fat as possible), then pour strained, defatted sauce back into pot. Discard aromatic vegetables. Stir in remaining {{1/4 cup}} orange juice. You should have about {{3 cups}} total braising liquid; if not, simmer until reduced to {{3 cups}}. Whisk in just enough of cornstarch mixture to slightly thicken sauce, adding it in {{1 tbsp}} increments (you may not need the whole amount).

brief: Return ribs to sauce and coat well.
Top with scallions and grated orange zest, then serve.
steps.text: Return short ribs and reduced sauce to Dutch oven, coating short ribs well with sauce. Sprinkle with scallions and remaining grated orange zest and serve with mashed potatoes or polenta . Leftover ribs can be reheated before serving, or meat can be boned, shredded, tossed with braising liquid, and folded into tacos.

title: Braised Chinese-Style Short Ribs With Soy, Orange, and 5-Spice Powder
